sections.overview: Described in 1989, this small cichlid is known from the Sipaliwini and middle Corantijn drainages of Suriname, with a possible occurrence in the Essequibo basin. Kullander and Nijssen included it in their 1989 monograph on Suriname cichlids.
sections.identification: A dark band through the eye and a marked flank pattern give the species its diagnostic appearance. A Smithsonian paratype record documents a shallow Corantijn tributary locality.
sections.habitat: It inhabits warm freshwater streams and river margins in the Guiana Shield. A Smithsonian paratype was collected at 0–1 m depth in a Corantijn stream.
sections.diet: A specialist account describes it as a benthic, sand-sifting omnivore; prey details are not established by the species summary.
sections.behavior: FishBase classifies it as benthopelagic, a broad habitat label rather than a detailed account of social behaviour.
sections.reproduction: An aquarium specialist describes biparental concealed substrate spawning, but this account is not a field study.
sections.ecology: It belongs to the Guianacara lineage, distinct from Geophagus; compare the nearby Suriname-basin G. brokopondo and G. winemilleri profiles for related eartheaters with different group placement.
sections.conservation: FishBase lists Least Concern, assessed on 28 December 2020.
